### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/service-settings`, touching **30** documentable anchor(s).

**5** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/data-modeling/drivers.mdx`  _(via SettingsService (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/kernel/runtime-services/settings-service.mdx`  _(via setMany (symbol, a method of class SettingsService))_
- `content/docs/permissions/authorization.mdx`  _(via registerLastAdminGuard (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/config-resolution.mdx`  _(via SettingsService (symbol, a top-level class), setMany (symbol, a method of class SettingsService))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/index.mdx`  _(via SettingsService (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v14.mdx`  _(via setMany (symbol, a method of class SettingsService))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **48** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 54df640b388c66153ba1e52c9ccc0082293358fa` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `5f3f70cf433a4880b14993344b190dde6d0c976b` — the merge of head `264c7ef59f163b75c02659b09e719298c059b0e8` into base `54df640b388c66153ba1e52c9ccc0082293358fa`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 5f3f70cf433a4880b14993344b190dde6d0c976b && git checkout 5f3f70cf433a4880b14993344b190dde6d0c976b
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 54df640b388c66153ba1e52c9ccc0082293358fa 264c7ef59f163b75c02659b09e719298c059b0e8 && git checkout -B drift-repro 54df640b388c66153ba1e52c9ccc0082293358fa && git merge --no-ff 264c7ef59f163b75c02659b09e719298c059b0e8

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 54df640b388c66153ba1e52c9ccc0082293358fa
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 54df640b388c66153ba1e52c9ccc0082293358fa` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `264c7ef59f163b75c02659b09e719298c059b0e8`
Local-runs: none

Seat read on the declaration face. The PR declares `Clause-②: yes (widening)` (new core security exports), with no narrowing, no published schema and no governed path (0 of 12 paths). The read covers the net diff against `main` (12 files, +694 / −120), the measurement 6354428826, the seat's rulings on it and the claim amendment 6354903470, the os-dev-report 6356012837, and the check-runs on this head.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The anchor rule, one definition: right, with no behaviour change.**
   - The new export is `organizationAnchorsPlatformStanding(grantOrganizationId, { walled, defaultOrganizationId })`: false under a wall or with no Default Organization, else a non-null owner equal to the Default Organization's id.
   - **Core** (`grantAnchorsPlatformStanding`) passes `grantOrganizationOf(grant)`, exactly as main compared it.
   - **The last-administrator guard** (`anchorOwnerTest`) passes its link owner over the simulated Default Organization. Main's `!walled` gate is now the predicate's `walled`; the answer is identical.
   - **The promotion** (`isAnchorHumanHolder`) passes a string-or-null owner and keeps its `user_id !== SYSTEM` exclusion. Under a wall main already passed an undefined Default Organization and returned early; the explicit `walled` flag states that, and the other caller passes `walled: false` with the same owner read as main.
2. **The organization-reach rule, one definition: right, with no behaviour change.**
   - `resolveOrganizationReach`, `organizationReachRowOwner` and `organizationReachAdmits`, with `organizationIdOf` as the one normalizer.
   - **`service-settings`:** own, walled-unowned, derived, and `no-organization-object` when no source is bound. The unbound-source case stays as main (#25249 owns it). The row filter and the write owner are equal to main in every branch.
   - **Core's localization fallback:** the requested posture's wall (R-1) and its catch that answers unowned on a failed derivation (R-2) are kept, as ruled, and named at the call site.
3. **Kept differences:** A-1 and A-2 (the normalizers) and R-1 and R-2. Each is named at its call site, and each is the stricter reading in the reader that keeps it. No answer changes.
4. **Pins and ablation:**
   - shared-predicate tables for both rules;
   - two new reader pins for the row predicate, which no existing pin exercised;
   - a diverged predicate reds every reader's pins, per the dev's ablation;
   - the existing pins of each reader are unchanged and green in CI.
5. **New public surface:** the core security index exports the two predicate modules. These are pure functions with no state, read by in-repo readers.

### ② Semver level

- **Changeset:** `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `@objectstack/plugin-security` and `@objectstack/service-settings` at `patch`; `Clause-②: yes (widening)`; `Metadata-protocol: none`; it says "no behaviour change".
- **`yes (widening)` is right:** new exports from core's public security index, and nothing narrowed.
- **`patch` is right** under the house rule. `Check Changeset` is success on this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- The third anchor copy, in `bootstrap-platform-admin.ts`, was folded under the claim amendment 6354903470. The file is not in PR #25311's diff, which has since merged.
- R-1 and R-2 were not converged, as ruled. Converging them would be a semantic change for a card of its own, and none is wanted: both are fail-stricter where they stand.
- Memoizing the localization fallback's `sys_organization` probe was optional and is not taken. It is bounded, and the ledger item 6353870843 is closed by this card's fold.
- R1, R4 and the harness were measured by the dev on this head (see the ACCEPT). The labelled harness lane is success on this head.

## Seat check

- **Shape:** 12 files, +694 / −120, across core security, plugin-auth's last-administrator guard, plugin-security's promotion and `service-settings`, plus one changeset. `check-governed-merges --pr 25352`: not governed, so this is an ordinary queue landing. `needs:upgrade-harness` is applied (tenancy reads in core security), and the labelled lane is green on this head.
- **Review tier:** `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, so the declaration face at `TIER_DEFAULT`. Seat record 6356253282 on this head: PASS.
  - Every reader's call site was read against `main`: three anchor readers and two reach readers. Each gives the same answer as main in every branch.
- **What it does:** one exported definition each, in core security, for the two rules:
  - the `admin_full_access` anchor rule (`organizationAnchorsPlatformStanding`);
  - the organization-reach rule (`resolveOrganizationReach`, `organizationReachRowOwner`, `organizationReachAdmits`).
  Every reader that spelled them now calls them. The kept differences (A-1, A-2, R-1, R-2) are named at their call sites. There is no behaviour change.
- **CI on the head:** 46 check-runs, every one success or skipped, including `Test Core`, `Build Core`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Check Changeset` and the labelled `18.x upgrade harness (opt-in)` lane. Mergeable clean. `main` is merged in at `54df640b38`.
- **R1–R4,** measured by the dev on this head:
  - R1: a production `os serve` under `single` on a fresh store: health, sign-up, sign-in and `me/localization` 200, and the first user holds `platform_admin`.
  - R4: under `isolated` and `group`, the same 200s; the configured owner holds `platform_admin`. Under `isolated`, a tenant localization PUT (Asia/Tokyo) reads back.
  - R2 and R3: the harness passed 16/16, both fixture legs. Dispatch gates: 74/74.
- **Changeset:** four packages at `patch`, `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, "no behaviour change". Right under the house rule.
- **Ledger:** this closes the #15212 ledger items 6348725929 (the anchor predicate spelled twice; three times, as measured) and the reach half of 6353870843.
- **Landing:** the seat flips the PR ready and enables auto-merge. `Fixes #25315` closes the card. #15212 then waits on #25249 alone.
